samples.summary: New `/auth` log-redaction helper `logSafeUrl` has no test at all (and is unexported, so it cannot be tested)
samples.evidence: `logSafeUrl` implements a security-motivated behavior (replace the query string of any `/auth` URL with `?<redacted>`, keep the query elsewhere) with a non-trivial regex `/^\/auth(?:\/|$)/` and a non-string passthrough. There is no `packages/backend/src/app.module.spec.ts` (Glob over `packages/backend/src/**/*.spec.ts` lists none) and a repo-wide grep for `logSafeUrl` returns only app.module.ts:34/87 plus a prose mention in docs/design/rest-api.md:396. Nothing exercises the boundary cases the comment claims (`/authors?x=1` must NOT be redacted; `/auth` with no query; a non-string url). The function is also module-private, so a regression here is invisible to every lane.
searchedFor: grep for 'app.module' in backend spec files

samples.summary: The renamed `__cliStateToken` → `__oauthState` handoff from guard to strategy is not covered by any test
samples.evidence: `GitHubStrategy.authenticate` now reads `req.__oauthState` and copies it into `opts.state`; `github-auth.guard.ts:111,116` is the only writer. github.strategy.spec.ts only asserts endpoint URLs — it never calls `authenticate` or inspects `opts.state`. A grep for `__oauthState`/`__cliStateToken` across packages/backend finds matches only in the guard, the guard spec, the strategy source and a controller comment — no test asserts the strategy forwards it. If the two ever disagree (a half-applied rename), the authorization request would reach GitHub with no `state` at all (passport-oauth2's NullStore always verifies), i.e. no CSRF binding, and the whole backend suite would still be green.

samples.summary: Browser state cookie attributes (httpOnly, secure, sameSite, path '/auth', maxAge) are never asserted — the test's `res.cookie` stub discards the options argument
samples.evidence: `contextFor` stubs the response as `cookie: (name, value) => cookies.push({ name, value })`, dropping the third argument. The test at line 154 (‘mints a cookie-backed `state`’) therefore asserts only the name and value. `startWebState` (github-auth.guard.ts) sets `httpOnly`, `secure`, `sameSite: 'lax'`, `path: '/auth'`, `maxAge` — all load-bearing for the double-submit (a wrong `path` means the cookie is never sent back on the callback, a `sameSite: 'strict'` likewise) and none of them can fail a test. The controller spec asserts `path: '/auth'` only on `clearCookie`, not on the set.

samples.summary: The 'state cookie is cleared whether or not it matched' behavior is only asserted on the success path
samples.evidence: auth.controller.ts's `verifyCallbackState` clears `OAUTH_STATE_COOKIE` before comparing, with the comment 'Single use: the cookie goes whether or not it matched.' The success test (line 343) asserts `clearCookie`, but the mismatch test (line 349) and the missing-cookie test (line 378) assert only `redirect`/`cookie` were not called — neither asserts `clearCookie`. Moving the clear after the equality check (so a failed attempt leaves the cookie replayable) would keep the whole suite green.
searchedFor: read auth.controller.spec.ts githubAuthCallback — browser flow block

samples.summary: The `command: commandPath(this)` wiring into the import/upload/download orchestrators is untested for every one of those commands
samples.evidence: `runFilesUpload`, `runFilesDownload`, `runDocsImport`, `runNotesImport`, `runSlidesImport` gained a `command` arg that the actions supply. The unit suites for those orchestrators (files-upload.test.ts, files-download.test.ts, docs-import.test.ts, notes-import.test.ts, slides-import.test.ts) never pass or assert `command` — grep for `command` in docs-import.test.ts and notes-content.test.ts returns nothing, and files-upload.test.ts only does `expect(err.join('')).toContain('HTTP_ERROR')`. The end-to-end attribution assertions in output.test.ts cover only `docs.get`, `sheets.cells.get`, `docs.content` and `schema`. Dropping `command: commandPath(this)` from any of these five action sites would fail nothing.
searchedFor: read the new assertions in packages/cli/test/output.test.ts

samples.summary: The new `sawUnboundCode` timeout message and the browser-open-failure URL printing branch are untested
samples.evidence: startCallbackServer sets `sawUnboundCode` when a callback arrives with no `state`, and the 30s timeout then emits a distinct 'Login callback carried no `state`' diagnostic; login-callback.test.ts exercises the 400 responses but never drives the timeout (fake timers would make it reachable), so the whole branch — including the flag being set only for `state === null` — is dead as far as tests go. Likewise the `if (!opened)` path that prints the secret-carrying authorization URL with the 'do not share' warning is never exercised: the `open` module mock always resolves, and the only related assertion is the negative `notices.some(n => n.includes('nonce=')) === false` on the success path.
searchedFor: grep 'sawUnboundCode|Could not open a browser' across packages/cli

samples.summary: `codeForStatus`'s HTTP_ERROR branch (exit code 1) has no test
samples.evidence: login-callback.test.ts covers the 401 → UNAUTHORIZED/exit 2 and 502 → SYSTEM/exit 2 rows, but no test drives a 4xx that is neither 401 nor 403 (e.g. 400/429), which is the only path that yields `HTTP_ERROR` and `process.exit(1)`. The exit-code split introduced by this change is therefore half-covered.
searchedFor: read the new login-callback.test.ts cases in the diff

samples.summary: 'stores no CLI state for a non-CLI request or an out-of-range port' leans on a trivially-true lookup
samples.evidence: Both assertions are `store.consumeState(req.__oauthState)` where `__oauthState` is by then the web token `w.<random>` — an unknown key, so `consumeState` returns `undefined` no matter what the guard did with the query. It would also pass if `__oauthState` were left undefined. The test does still catch the specific regression of a CLI state being minted (the token would then resolve), but it asserts nothing about the port/mode gate beyond that, and reads as stronger coverage than it is.

finding.summary: New `/auth` log-redaction helper `logSafeUrl` has no test at all (and is unexported, so it cannot be tested)
finding.evidence: `logSafeUrl` implements a security-motivated behavior (replace the query string of any `/auth` URL with `?<redacted>`, keep the query elsewhere) with a non-trivial regex `/^\/auth(?:\/|$)/` and a non-string passthrough. There is no `packages/backend/src/app.module.spec.ts` (Glob over `packages/backend/src/**/*.spec.ts` lists none) and a repo-wide grep for `logSafeUrl` returns only app.module.ts:34/87 plus a prose mention in docs/design/rest-api.md:396. verdict.reason: Verified independently: `logSafeUrl` exists at packages/backend/src/app.module.ts:34-40 as a module-private helper used only by the pino `req` serializer at line 87, and no test anywhere exercises it. Repo-wide greps for `logSafeUrl`, `redact`, `?<redacted>`, `authors?`, `serializers`, `pinoHttp`, and name variants (`safeUrl|sanitizeUrl|scrubUrl|maskUrl|stripQuery`) produce no test hit; the only `isSafeUrl` tests (packages/core/test/url.test.ts) cover unrelated protocol gating. Glob of all 59 packages/backend/**/*.{spec,test}.ts shows no app.module spec, and the only backend spec mentioning app.module (throttler.spec.ts:33,101) does so in comments about throttler buckets. The e2e suite in packages/backend/test/ contains no log assertions, and access logging is disabled outright under NODE_ENV=test (app.module.ts:50-52), so e2e cannot cover it indirectly either. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a new behavior with non-trivial boundary logic (`/^\/auth(?:\/|$)/` prefix boundary, `?` split, non-string passthrough) shipped with no meaningful test at all — major.

finding.summary: The renamed `__cliStateToken` → `__oauthState` handoff from guard to strategy is not covered by any test
finding.evidence: `GitHubStrategy.authenticate` now reads `req.__oauthState` and copies it into `opts.state`; `github-auth.guard.ts:111,116` is the only writer. github.strategy.spec.ts only asserts endpoint URLs — it never calls `authenticate` or inspects `opts.state`. A grep for `__oauthState`/`__cliStateToken` across packages/backend finds matches only in the guard, the guard spec, the strategy source and a controller comment — no test asserts the strategy forwards it. If the two ever disagree (a half-applied rename), the authorization request would reach GitHub with no `state` at all (passport-oauth2's NullStore always verifies), i.e. no CSRF binding, and the whole backend suite would still be green.

verdict.reason: The reader side of the handoff is real: github.strategy.ts:61-68 overrides authenticate() to copy req.__oauthState into opts.state, guarding CSRF binding (the comment notes passport-oauth2's NullStore.verify always succeeds without state). No test exercises it. github.strategy.spec.ts (read in full) has 5 tests, all routed through the endpoints() helper that only reads _oauth2._authorizeUrl/_accessTokenUrl/_userProfileURL/_userEmailURL; it never builds a request, never calls authenticate, never inspects opts.state. The guard spec cannot cover it either: github-auth.guard.spec.ts:37-46 stubs the Passport base canActivate with jest.spyOn(...).mockReturnValue(true), so the strategy is never invoked, and its assertions only read back what the guard wrote (lines 56, 140, 148, 158, 171, 183). I searched well beyond the reviewer's greps for a counterexample: repo-wide GitHubStrategy|github\.strategy references (only that one spec among tests); all backend spec/e2e files for `authenticate`, `opts.state`, `state=`, `oauth/authorize`, and `Location`/`headers.location` (no hits driving an authorization start); packages/backend/test/** for `github` (only CI comments and setAuthEnvDefaults in integration-helpers.ts:88-95, no e2e hitting GET /auth/github); repo-wide `/auth/github` (frontend link, CLI, docs, README only); and confirmed no separate e2e suite exists (no /e2e dir; frontend and CLI suites don't touch the backend strategy — packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts tests the CLI's own localhost callback nonce). The coverage is asymmetric: a guard-side rename would be caught by the guard spec's literal req.__oauthState reads, but a strategy-side rename or a dropped override is caught by nothing and the suite stays green while requests reach GitHub with no state. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a changed, security-relevant behavior with no meaningful test — major.

searchedFor: grep for createState/createCode usages in backend auth specs
read cli-auth.store.ts to confirm arg order
finding.summary: No test covers the PKCE challenge flowing from the consumed state into the minted code — the whole protection could be silently disabled and the suite stays green
finding.evidence: auth.controller.ts:126 is the only place `state.codeChallenge` is carried onto the authorization code (`createCode(user.id, state.codeChallenge)`). Every test of that path in auth.controller.spec.ts creates state without a challenge: line 193 `createState('cli', 9876)` and line 221 `createState('cli', 9876, 'n0nce-x/y')` (third arg is the nonce, not the challenge), and neither test then redeems the resulting code. The `PKCE binding` describe (spec lines 347–410) bypasses the callback entirely by calling `cliAuthStore.createCode(42, challenge)` directly. So if the controller were changed to `createCode(user.id)` — dropping the challenge and turning every CLI code back into a bearer — no test in the repo fails. Likewise github-auth.guard.spec.ts only asserts the challenge reaches the store, never that it reaches a code. The end-to-end binding (guard → state → code → exchange) is untested.

verdict.reason: A test covering exactly this end-to-end binding exists: auth.controller.spec.ts:237-282 ("carries the login`s PKCE challenge onto the code it mints"). It creates CLI state carrying a real S256 challenge via createState('cli', 9876, undefined, challenge) — and cli-auth.store.ts:42-47 confirms the 4th positional arg is codeChallenge, so the challenge is genuinely stored — then invokes the real controller.githubAuthCallback against a real (unmocked) CliAuthStore (spec:41), extracts the code from the redirect URL, asserts consumeCode(code,'not-the-verifier') is undefined (spec:264), and then, with a second callback run, asserts consumeCode(code2, verifier) === mockUser.id (spec:266-281). If auth.controller.ts:140 were changed to createCode(user.id) (dropping the challenge), the code would be unchallenged and consumeCode(code2, verifier) would return undefined per cli-auth.store.ts:122-123, so line 281 would fail. The complementary unchallenged path is pinned at spec:284-300. The reviewer's cited line numbers (PKCE binding at 347-410; it is actually at 482-545) do not match the working tree, indicating they inspected a stale version of the spec.
